top_three.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
top_three.title_en: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
top_three.author: The Verge AI
top_three.article_content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”

I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.

“Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”

Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”

“I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”

Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.

Of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.

“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he said.

top_three.article_content_zh:
微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 表示，他对 AGI 很着迷，至少在人工智能可能如何对经济结构产生惊人的变化以及政治可能因此而发生变化时是这样。 “我是 AGI 的受害者，在经济层面上，围绕 AGI 的政治经济学组织是什么？”他在旧金山大通中心的 Microsoft Ignite 主题演讲后的圆桌讨论中问道。

但纳德拉并不认为像克劳德这样的前沿模型是有意识的。他说：“我不这么认为。”他补充说，他遵循微软人工智能首席执行官穆斯塔法·苏莱曼（Mustafa Suleyman）的观点，即公司不应赋予模型权利，并像对待他们可能具有道德地位一样对待他们，而像 Anthropic 这样的公司则将其视为原则问题。苏莱曼告诉我，他认为 Anthropic 的团队已经“头脑简单”了，这种做法很危险。

纳德拉对此并没有那么坚定。 “这是一场很好的辩论，”他说。 “我对此并不教条。我想说的是，我们必须处理的最重要的社会技术问题是如何确保经济体能够广泛传播这项技术？”

在听到纳德拉回答另一位记者关于 Anthropic 在其办公套件中发布更多产品的问题后，我问纳德拉他如何看待人工智能。纳德拉详细讨论了如果允许一种人工智能模型获得垄断地位，经济可能会崩溃，民主也会终结。

“大多数人认为这是科技公司之间的竞争，当然事实确实如此，”他说。 “但请记住，这种模式没有限制。它将是一家医疗保健公司。它可以是一家金融服务公司。如果它愿意的话，它可以是任何东西。它可以接管政府。将其视为科技公司之间的某种狭隘竞争，谁将达到下一个万亿美元的市值，是最奇怪、最狭隘的思考方式之一。”

纳德拉接着表示，未来公司的本质将被颠覆。 “如果情报具有网络效应，那么企业的未来是什么？”他问道。 “如果模型看到任何东西并学习它，并且基本上所有人力资本都崩溃为代币资本，那么公司和公司中的人力资本的作用是什么？这就是争论。”

“我认为在这种背景下，政治经济将会变得越来越有趣。如果这样下去，如果只有资本而没有劳动力，那么没有人——至少在民主国家——甚至可以赢得选举。我的意思是，我不知道，这不是一种经济。”

“如果马克思主义的观点是只有一家公司，那么一切都结束了，对吗？对我们所有人来说。不仅仅是我。你也会以某种方式成为 Anthropic 的某个附属公司。”

不用说，这并不是科技公司首席执行官通常谈论推出竞争性电子表格软件的方式。

当然，纳德拉还在Ignite上推广了微软的各种人工智能工具，这些工具承诺让企业客户为各种任务选择最具成本效益的模型，运行自己的模型，并以不同的方式控制自己的数据。这里的想法是，市场将需要许多不同类型的模型和主权数据，以防止控制中心化，这是纳德拉在我们讲话时不断提到的主题。

“我认为，如果你相信世界经济需要的不仅仅是一两家公司，那么根据定义，某种类型的公司就需要有同样多的模型，”他说。

top_three.title: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
top_three.title_en: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
top_three.author: TechCrunch
top_three.article_content:
Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue.

In the long term, the company may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Meanwhile,Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China.

That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the new rules. If large data centers suited for training AI models want to buy Nvidia chips, they will have to certify they aren’t serving any Chinese customers, export control attorney Dan Fisher-Owens told TechCrunch.

If they can’t provide that certification, the new rules may force them toward other chip options and further eat into Nvidia’s market share.

top_three.title_zh: 英伟达停止对华供应H200芯片
top_three.summary_zh: 英伟达代理CEO Colette Kress宣布停止向中国销售H200芯片，终止此前经黄仁勋与特朗普斡旋达成的高关税出口协议
top_three.article_content_zh:
英伟达代理首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)周二表示，英伟达将不再在中国销售其H200芯片，从而结束该公司参与美国禁止向中国销售先进芯片的一项有争议的漏洞。

自首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋上周卸任以来，中国获得领先人工智能加速器的机会是该公司首次财报电话会议上的一个重要话题。就在这一消息披露的同一天，英伟达宣布将成立一个董事会级委员会来监督国家安全政策、出口管制合规性和全球贸易风险。

英伟达在中国销售 H200 芯片的交易是由黄仁勋和唐纳德·特朗普总统促成的。该安排要求芯片通过美国运输，从而允许政府征收 25% 的关税。

这一途径激怒了对华鹰派，他们想要否认中国实验室的计算能力并保持美国在人工智能领域的领先地位，但黄长期以来认为，美国在中国竞争更重要。今年四月，他对播客 Dwarkesh Patel 表示，“承认美国科技行业的市场对我们的国家来说是一种伤害。”

黄仁勋被免职的部分原因是与一家因走私芯片到中国而受到调查的公司首席执行官的风流韵事，恰逢周一发布的新规定，禁止先进的美国芯片进入为中国客户提供远程服务的外国数据中心。

投资银行 Jefferies 预测，这些规则可能会使 Nvidia 明年的数据中心收入减少 440 亿至 620 亿美元。在谈到新的出口管制时，克雷斯表示，对 Vera Rubin 等先进芯片的需求积压意味着这些规则不会对公司的营收产生影响。

长期来看，该公司可能面临新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印尼等潜在客户的流失。英伟达对中国依赖的批评者声称，其多达 20% 的收入来自与中国相关的需求——在英伟达停止披露这些数字之前，其新加坡子公司的年收入在 2025 年达到 1040 亿美元——但这种情况显然将会改变。

甚至在 Nvidia 决定停止发货 H200 之前，中国基本上就拒绝接受其交付。乔治城安全与新兴技术中心研究员雅各布·费尔德戈斯 (Jacob Feldgoise) 表示，即使主要的人工智能计算用户想要仍然先进的 Nvidia 设备，政府也更愿意为国内芯片行业创造需求。

与此同时，中国前沿实验室正在寻找在其他地方获取英伟达芯片的方法。所有中国领先的人工智能模型都有证据显示，它们都接受过禁止出口到中国的 Nvidia Grace Blackwell 芯片的训练。

这些培训可能是在中国境外的数据中心进行的，但根据新规定，将禁止向这些设施销售。出口管制律师 Dan Fisher-Owens 告诉 TechCrunch，如果适合训练人工智能模型的大型数据中心想要购买 Nvidia 芯片，他们必须证明自己不为任何中国客户提供服务。

如果他们无法提供该认证，新规则可能会迫使他们选择其他芯片，并进一步蚕食英伟达的市场份额。

top_three.title_en: Sources detail how the Microsoft 365 outage began in Switzerland and spread as failover systems shifted traffic, leaving 80%+ of Exchange servers unresponsive (Tom Warren/The Verge)
top_three.author: The Verge
top_three.article_content:
At 9AM last Thursday, everything seemed normal. Microsoft employees were arriving on campus, ready for a regular day of emails and meetings. But barely an hour later, one of Microsoft’s worst outages in history started to unfold, leaving employees, businesses, and many governments without access to Outlook emails for nearly 24 hours.

It all started in Switzerland, according to a source familiar with the outage. Exchange Online servers that power Outlook started to fall offline. The problem quickly spread to Mexico, and then to other countries around the world, as Microsoft’s failover systems tried to shift email traffic elsewhere. Within a couple of hours, more than 80 percent of Exchange servers were unresponsive.

tell me that Microsoft marked the outage as “sev0” in its internal incident tracking system, the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Hundreds of engineers began trying to figure out what had gone wrong, and how to restore service. It’s not unusual for servers to fail under certain circumstances, but Microsoft has a variety of systems that are supposed to route traffic toward healthy servers to keep the broader system online. In this case, the failover systems did their job, but they also spread the problem.

In the early hours of the outage, engineers were analyzing crash reports, trace logs, and kernel dumps to try and find clues to the giant outage. Some servers had entered into maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads. Engineers tried to bring servers back online, but they were almost immediately overwhelmed by traffic waiting to access the servers.

Exchange servers boot up and run an OS over a network (Preboot Execution Environment), a process that allows Microsoft’s support staff and engineers to manage OS updates remotely. I understand that the sudden burst of traffic from servers being rebooted was overwhelming the systems monitoring them, causing a form of reboot loop where they kept trying and failing to come back online.

As engineers continued to hunt for the root cause, Microsoft was even struggling to roll back servers to a healthy state using its usual processes of reverting recent changes. As the outside world began to wonder if this outage was related to a cyberattack or sloppy AI coding, Microsoft’s engineers were already investigating potential attack vectors and liaising with DDoS specialists to understand whether this could have been an attack.

I’m told crash reports and logs quickly ruled out the possibility of an attack, and after recent rollbacks failed, Microsoft’s engineers began to take a closer look at the networking stack of the servers and discovered an unusual bug. It was unusual because the bug had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers.

“A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions,” wrote Charles Lamanna, the leader of Microsoft’s Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) team, in a post on X. The teams behind Office, Outlook, and Microsoft Teams all started reporting to Lamanna last month after the head of Office and Teams, Ryan Roslansky, left the company.

top_three.title_zh: 微软Exchange服务大规模宕机始末及技术失效机制
top_three.summary_zh: 微软Exchange Online因瑞士节点故障及自动故障转移机制触发网络拥塞，导致全球80%以上服务器陷入重启循环
top_three.article_content_zh:
上周四上午 9 点，一切看起来都很正常。微软员工抵达校园，准备开始一天的电子邮件和会议。但不到一个小时后，微软历史上最严重的故障之一开始发生，导致员工、企业和许多政府近 24 小时无法访问 Outlook 电子邮件。

这一切都始于瑞士。为 Outlook 提供支持的 Exchange Online 服务器开始脱机。由于微软的故障转移系统试图将电子邮件流量转移到其他地方，该问题迅速蔓延到墨西哥，然后蔓延到世界其他国家。几个小时内，超过 80% 的 Exchange 服务器没有响应。

消息人士告诉我，微软在其内部事件跟踪系统中将此次中断标记为“sev0”，这是最高级别，这表明服务中断已达到灾难性级别。数百名工程师开始试图找出问题所在以及如何恢复服务。服务器在某些情况下发生故障并不罕见，但微软有多种系统可以将流量路由到健康的服务器，以保持更广泛的系统在线。在这种情况下，故障转移系统发挥了作用，但也传播了问题。

在停电的最初几个小时，工程师们正在分析崩溃报告、跟踪日志和内核转储，试图找到这次大停电的线索。一些服务器已进入维护模式，并且由于 CPU 负载异常高而变得无响应。工程师试图让服务器重新上线，但他们几乎立即就被等待访问服务器的流量淹没了。

Exchange 服务器通过网络（预启动执行环境）启动并运行操作系统，该过程允许 Microsoft 的支持人员和工程师远程管理操作系统更新。据我所知，重新启动的服务器突然爆发的流量压垮了监控它们的系统，导致了一种重新启动循环，它们不断尝试但无法重新上线。

当工程师继续寻找根本原因时，微软甚至正在努力使用恢复最近更改的常规流程将服务器恢复到健康状态。当外界开始怀疑这次中断是否与网络攻击或草率的人工智能编码有关时，微软的工程师已经在调查潜在的攻击向量，并与 DDoS 专家联络，以了解这是否可能是一次攻击。

我被告知崩溃报告和日志很快就排除了攻击的可能性，在最近的回滚失败后，微软的工程师开始仔细研究服务器的网络堆栈，并发现了一个不寻常的错误。这是不寻常的，因为该错误自 7 月份以来一直存在于 Microsoft 365 网络网关服务器上，没有对服务器产生任何影响。

微软 Copilot、代理和平台 (CAP) 团队负责人 Charles Lamanna 在 X 上的一篇帖子中写道：“潜在缺陷导致服务器在某些负载条件下变得不堪重负且无响应。”上个月，在 Office 和 Teams 负责人 Ryan Roslansky 离开公司后，Office、Outlook 和 Microsoft Teams 背后的团队都开始向 Lamanna 汇报。

微软的初步事件后报告将该错误描述为“由于内部 Windows 进程内的锁争用”而影响特定 Windows 服务器的错误。该错误不会影响常规版本的 Windows，因为它是专门为 Microsoft 365 网络网关服务器准备的修复的结果。

微软直到这次重大中断才发现这个错误，它承认这是由于其测试实验室中使用的流量混合和硬件造成的。 “在具有更多内核和较新硬件的机器上，争用问题会更加严重；而我们的负载测试往往侧重于内核较少的较弱硬件，”拉曼纳写道。

由于另外两起增加负载并减少服务器容量的事件，该错误变得明显。在此 Outlook 中断开始前 15 小时，Microsoft Teams 从备用网络网关故障转移到支持 Exchange Online 的主网关。 “这增加了网关的负载并改变了其流量模式，”拉曼纳写道。通常这不会是一个问题，但与此同时，该网关大约 14% 的服务器容量“由于前一天的不相关问题而停止服务”。

bug、Microsoft Teams 故障转移和服务器容量减少这三重因素都导致网络网关触发了自 7 月份以来一直处于休眠状态的问题。微软花了近 24 小时才使其 Exchange 服务器再次稳定下来，而且我获悉，试图解决问题的团队有时会进行重叠干预，从而使协调变得复杂。

微软工程师一直在进行桥牌通话，参与人数一度达到了 1000 人的上限。这向您展示了有多少团队参与试图找到这次大规模中断的根本原因，该中断始于美国的流量高峰期。

拉曼纳写道：“恢复时间比平时要长，因为当服务器恢复服务时，它们立即被等待的流量淹没，再次变得无响应。” “我们通常的自动恢复流程并不是为了从这种广泛的无响应状态恢复服务。此外，由于主要代码缺陷是几个月前的潜在错误，因此我们的正常回滚、飞行和功能标志无法快速恢复更改。”

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软Exchange Online服务因瑞士服务器集群异常触发内部sev0级事故，自动故障转移机制（Failover）将流量导向非故障服务器，导致全球超80%的Exchange服务器因CPU过载陷入重启循环。微软工程团队通过内核日志排查发现，服务器在网络启动预引导环境（PXE）重连过程中遭遇瞬时流量洪峰，导致系统进入连锁性的服务恢复死锁。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft's Exchange Online service suffered a sev0-rated outage initiated by server failures in Switzerland, which triggered failover mechanisms that propagated the issue, leaving over 80% of Exchange servers unresponsive. The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次事件揭示了超大规模云架构中‘自动化故障转移’机制的负反馈效应：当系统规模超过临界点，自动容灾脚本可能演变为分布式拒绝服务（DDoS）攻击效应，导致基础设施雪崩。对于高度依赖微软生产力套件的企业而言，过度集中的后端架构缺乏多云冗余，在极端失效场景下已构成系统性操作风险。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the negative feedback loops inherent in large-scale automated failover mechanisms, where recovery protocols can inadvertently act as a self-inflicted DDoS attack during system saturation. The event underscores the systemic operational risk of centralized cloud dependencies and the urgent need for multi-cloud redundancy in critical enterprise communication workflows.

news.title: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
news.title_en: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
news.author: TechCrunch
news.article_content:
Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue.

In the long term, the company may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Meanwhile,Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China.

That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the new rules. If large data centers suited for training AI models want to buy Nvidia chips, they will have to certify they aren’t serving any Chinese customers, export control attorney Dan Fisher-Owens told TechCrunch.

If they can’t provide that certification, the new rules may force them toward other chip options and further eat into Nvidia’s market share.

news.title_zh: 英伟达停止对华供应H200芯片
news.summary_zh: 英伟达代理CEO Colette Kress宣布停止向中国销售H200芯片，终止此前经黄仁勋与特朗普斡旋达成的高关税出口协议
news.article_content_zh:
英伟达代理首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)周二表示，英伟达将不再在中国销售其H200芯片，从而结束该公司参与美国禁止向中国销售先进芯片的一项有争议的漏洞。

自首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋上周卸任以来，中国获得领先人工智能加速器的机会是该公司首次财报电话会议上的一个重要话题。就在这一消息披露的同一天，英伟达宣布将成立一个董事会级委员会来监督国家安全政策、出口管制合规性和全球贸易风险。

英伟达在中国销售 H200 芯片的交易是由黄仁勋和唐纳德·特朗普总统促成的。该安排要求芯片通过美国运输，从而允许政府征收 25% 的关税。

这一途径激怒了对华鹰派，他们想要否认中国实验室的计算能力并保持美国在人工智能领域的领先地位，但黄长期以来认为，美国在中国竞争更重要。今年四月，他对播客 Dwarkesh Patel 表示，“承认美国科技行业的市场对我们的国家来说是一种伤害。”

黄仁勋被免职的部分原因是与一家因走私芯片到中国而受到调查的公司首席执行官的风流韵事，恰逢周一发布的新规定，禁止先进的美国芯片进入为中国客户提供远程服务的外国数据中心。

投资银行 Jefferies 预测，这些规则可能会使 Nvidia 明年的数据中心收入减少 440 亿至 620 亿美元。在谈到新的出口管制时，克雷斯表示，对 Vera Rubin 等先进芯片的需求积压意味着这些规则不会对公司的营收产生影响。

长期来看，该公司可能面临新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印尼等潜在客户的流失。英伟达对中国依赖的批评者声称，其多达 20% 的收入来自与中国相关的需求——在英伟达停止披露这些数字之前，其新加坡子公司的年收入在 2025 年达到 1040 亿美元——但这种情况显然将会改变。

甚至在 Nvidia 决定停止发货 H200 之前，中国基本上就拒绝接受其交付。乔治城安全与新兴技术中心研究员雅各布·费尔德戈斯 (Jacob Feldgoise) 表示，即使主要的人工智能计算用户想要仍然先进的 Nvidia 设备，政府也更愿意为国内芯片行业创造需求。

与此同时，中国前沿实验室正在寻找在其他地方获取英伟达芯片的方法。所有中国领先的人工智能模型都有证据显示，它们都接受过禁止出口到中国的 Nvidia Grace Blackwell 芯片的训练。

这些培训可能是在中国境外的数据中心进行的，但根据新规定，将禁止向这些设施销售。出口管制律师 Dan Fisher-Owens 告诉 TechCrunch，如果适合训练人工智能模型的大型数据中心想要购买 Nvidia 芯片，他们必须证明自己不为任何中国客户提供服务。

如果他们无法提供该认证，新规则可能会迫使他们选择其他芯片，并进一步蚕食英伟达的市场份额。

当您通过我们文章中的链接购买时，我们可能会赚取少量佣金。这并不影响我们的编辑独立性。

news.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
news.title_en: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”

I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.

“Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”

Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”

“I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”

Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.

Of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.

“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he said.

news.article_content_zh:
微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 表示，他对 AGI 很着迷，至少在人工智能可能如何对经济结构产生惊人的变化以及政治可能因此而发生变化时是这样。 “我是 AGI 的受害者，在经济层面上，围绕 AGI 的政治经济学组织是什么？”他在旧金山大通中心的 Microsoft Ignite 主题演讲后的圆桌讨论中问道。

但纳德拉并不认为像克劳德这样的前沿模型是有意识的。他说：“我不这么认为。”他补充说，他遵循微软人工智能首席执行官穆斯塔法·苏莱曼（Mustafa Suleyman）的观点，即公司不应赋予模型权利，并像对待他们可能具有道德地位一样对待他们，而像 Anthropic 这样的公司则将其视为原则问题。苏莱曼告诉我，他认为 Anthropic 的团队已经“头脑简单”了，这种做法很危险。

纳德拉对此并没有那么坚定。 “这是一场很好的辩论，”他说。 “我对此并不教条。我想说的是，我们必须处理的最重要的社会技术问题是如何确保经济体能够广泛传播这项技术？”

在听到纳德拉回答另一位记者关于 Anthropic 在其办公套件中发布更多产品的问题后，我问纳德拉他如何看待人工智能。纳德拉详细讨论了如果允许一种人工智能模型获得垄断地位，经济可能会崩溃，民主也会终结。

“大多数人认为这是科技公司之间的竞争，当然事实确实如此，”他说。 “但请记住，这种模式没有限制。它将是一家医疗保健公司。它可以是一家金融服务公司。如果它愿意的话，它可以是任何东西。它可以接管政府。将其视为科技公司之间的某种狭隘竞争，谁将达到下一个万亿美元的市值，是最奇怪、最狭隘的思考方式之一。”

纳德拉接着表示，未来公司的本质将被颠覆。 “如果情报具有网络效应，那么企业的未来是什么？”他问道。 “如果模型看到任何东西并学习它，并且基本上所有人力资本都崩溃为代币资本，那么公司和公司中的人力资本的作用是什么？这就是争论。”

“我认为在这种背景下，政治经济将会变得越来越有趣。如果这样下去，如果只有资本而没有劳动力，那么没有人——至少在民主国家——甚至可以赢得选举。我的意思是，我不知道，这不是一种经济。”

“如果马克思主义的观点是只有一家公司，那么一切都结束了，对吗？对我们所有人来说。不仅仅是我。你也会以某种方式成为 Anthropic 的某个附属公司。”

不用说，这并不是科技公司首席执行官通常谈论推出竞争性电子表格软件的方式。

当然，纳德拉还在Ignite上推广了微软的各种人工智能工具，这些工具承诺让企业客户为各种任务选择最具成本效益的模型，运行自己的模型，并以不同的方式控制自己的数据。这里的想法是，市场将需要许多不同类型的模型和主权数据，以防止控制中心化，这是纳德拉在我们讲话时不断提到的主题。

“我认为，如果你相信世界经济需要的不仅仅是一两家公司，那么根据定义，某种类型的公司就需要有同样多的模型，”他说。

news.title: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)
news.title_en: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)

inline_images.caption: Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

news.author: Axios
news.article_content:
Nvidia's interim CEO said Tuesday that the company will be "disciplined" as it decides how much to invest in neoclouds and other AI customers going forward.

Why it matters: Nvidia isn't just the biggest chip partner for AI startups — it's a major source of capital.

What they're saying: "Our momentum is real," interim CEO Colette Kress said on at the end of conference call with investors and analysts. "Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We've got this."

In particular, Kress said the company would continue to be "disciplined and selective in our support" for so-called neoclouds.

Zoom in: Kress didn't name-check any other specific customers but said the company would offer capital to suppliers to help them move quickly.

Catch-up quick: Huang resigned last week after revelations that he had a relationship with a woman who allegedly had ties to Chinese intelligence.

On the call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones through cold water on the notion of a quick return for Huang. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," he said.

news.title: Apple HomeView teardown: a step backward in repairability compared to recent iPads and HomePods, with heavily glued display, speakers, and logic board (Carsten Frauenheim/iFixit News)
news.title_en: Apple HomeView teardown: a step backward in repairability compared to recent iPads and HomePods, with heavily glued display, speakers, and logic board (Carsten Frauenheim/iFixit News)

inline_images.caption: HomeView laid out on a table
inline_images.alt: HomeView laid out on a table

news.author: iFixit News
news.article_content:
Apple’s first iPad-stuck-to-a-HomePod smarthome hub landed on our teardown table this week, and we figured we knew what we were getting into. We’ve taken apart plenty of iPads and HomePods. And lately, Apple has actually been getting better at making them repairable.

The original HomePod took a hacksaw to open, but by the second generation, we could get inside without destroying anything. Even the notoriously glue-heavy iPad has made progress: easier battery access, replaceable USB-C ports, and finally, official repair manuals. We were starting to think Apple had learned a few lessons.

Then we met HomeView. A 7-inch iPad display up top. A HomePod mini down below. A few screws holding the two together.

But that was an oversimplification. By the time we got it apart, we had ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with. The base showed some promising signs of HomePod DNA, but the display was a different story entirely.

So what happened? How did a company that’s been making real repairability improvements produce a device that’s so dead set against being fixed?

Before picking up a tool, we put the HomeView through our Lumafield Neptune CT scanner. At first glance, things looked pretty encouraging.

There’s a small circuit board near the top, flanked by antennas on either side, with what appear to be large speakers mounted toward the bottom.

The base is more densely packed, which made sense to us, since we expected to find HomePod mini guts in there and not much more besides maybe added weight.

A central pivot connects the display and the base, which look like two distinct assemblies. Surely we’d be able to separate them if one half needed replacing?

There was one familiar warning sign. Just like in an iPad, getting to anything behind the display meant going through the fragile front glass first.

Still, we’d dealt with that plenty of times before. What we hadn’t bargained for was just how determined Apple was to keep everything else from coming apart.

We’ve opened up enough iPads to know the basics: heat up the display, soften the adhesive, and carefully lift the screen.

The display fit our heat mat perfectly, but the aluminum enclosure was very good at carrying that heat away. The extra thermal mass meant for quite a long wait. Even so, the adhesive held on harder than on any Apple product we’ve opened recently. Why are we having an even harder time getting into something that spends its life sitting on a kitchen counter?

Once we finally lifted the display, we were quick to confirm that most of the internal space is occupied by those two enormous speakers. More on those later.

But first, an oddity. With the screen out of the way, we can get to the bracket covering the display’s press connector. One side of that bracket is held down with a Phillips screw. The other side uses Torx.

Could Apple have made both screws Phillips, or both Torx? Absolutely. Whether you care about efficient manufacturing or DIY repair, two driver types for a single bracket is a poor choice. Apple did this for years on iPhones. We didn’t get it then, and we don’t get it now.

It wasn’t the last time, either. The coaxial connectors for the two antennas are secured with Phillips screws, and then the camera bracket needs a larger Torx bit, so we spent the whole teardown juggling bits for no good reason.

news.summary_en: iFixit's teardown of the Apple HomeView reveals a heavy reliance on structural adhesives for its display, speakers, and logic board, marking a regressive step in modular design. Despite recent improvements in repairability across iPad and HomePod lines, HomeView’s integration forces high-risk disassembly that frequently leads to component failure.
news.title_zh: 苹果HomeView拆解：维修难度大幅回升
news.summary_zh: iFixit拆解显示，苹果新款智能家居设备HomeView内部高度依赖强力胶粘合，维修难度远超近年推出的iPad与HomePod产品线
news.article_content_zh:
苹果首款 iPad 固定在 HomePod 上的智能家居中心本周出现在我们的拆解台上，我们认为我们知道自己要做什么。我们拆解了大量的 iPad 和 HomePod。最近，苹果实际上在让它们变得可修复方面做得越来越好。

最初的 HomePod 需要用钢锯才能打开，但到了第二代，我们可以在不破坏任何东西的情况下进入内部。即使是出了名的使用大量胶水的 iPad 也取得了进步：更方便的电池使用、可更换的 USB-C 端口，以及最后的官方维修手册。我们开始认为苹果已经吸取了一些教训。

然后我们遇到了HomeView。顶部有一个 7 英寸的 iPad 显示屏。下面是一个 HomePod mini。几颗螺丝将两者固定在一起。

但这过于简单化了。当我们把它拆开时，我们已经扯断了一个连接器，将一个扬声器折断成两半，并对这块糟糕的逻辑板施加了比我们任何人都能接受的更大的力量。该底座显示出 HomePod DNA 的一些有希望的迹象，但展示的情况完全不同。

那么发生了什么？一家一直在进行真正的可修复性改进的公司是如何生产出如此坚决不肯修复的设备的？

在拿起工具之前，我们将 HomeView 通过 Lumafield Neptune CT 扫描仪。乍一看，事情看起来相当令人鼓舞。

顶部附近有一块小电路板，两侧都有天线，底部似乎安装有大型扬声器。

底座更加密集，这对我们来说很有意义，因为我们希望在其中找到 HomePod 迷你内胆，除了可能增加重量之外，没有更多东西。

中央枢轴连接显示器和底座，它们看起来像两个不同的组件。如果其中一半需要更换，我们肯定能够将它们分开吗？

有一个熟悉的警告标志。就像在 iPad 中一样，要接触显示屏后面的任何东西都需要先穿过易碎的前玻璃。

不过，我们之前已经处理过很多次了。我们没有预料到的是，苹果公司有多么坚决地阻止其他一切崩溃。

我们已经拆开足够多的 iPad 来了解基本知识：加热显示屏、软化粘合剂，然后小心地抬起屏幕。

显示屏非常适合我们的散热垫，但铝制外壳非常适合带走热量。额外的热质量意味着相当长的等待时间。即便如此，这种粘合剂的粘性比我们最近打开的任何苹果产品都要牢固。为什么我们更难接触那些终其一生都坐在厨房柜台上的东西？

一旦我们最终抬起显示器，我们很快就确认了大部分内部空间都被这两个巨大的扬声器占据了。稍后会详细介绍。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 拆解分析机构iFixit对苹果智能家居中心设备HomeView进行实物测绘，发现该产品内部核心组件（显示屏、扬声器及逻辑板）大量使用工业胶粘合，而非主流的模块化螺丝结构。尽管苹果近年在iPad与HomePod系列中改善了维修便捷性，但HomeView的反向设计策略导致拆解过程中极易引发连接器受损及组件物理断裂。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: iFixit's teardown of the Apple HomeView reveals a heavy reliance on structural adhesives for its display, speakers, and logic board, marking a regressive step in modular design. Despite recent improvements in repairability across iPad and HomePod lines, HomeView’s integration forces high-risk disassembly that frequently leads to component failure.

news.title: Sources detail how the Microsoft 365 outage began in Switzerland and spread as failover systems shifted traffic, leaving 80%+ of Exchange servers unresponsive (Tom Warren/The Verge)
news.title_en: Sources detail how the Microsoft 365 outage began in Switzerland and spread as failover systems shifted traffic, leaving 80%+ of Exchange servers unresponsive (Tom Warren/The Verge)
news.author: The Verge
news.article_content:
At 9AM last Thursday, everything seemed normal. Microsoft employees were arriving on campus, ready for a regular day of emails and meetings. But barely an hour later, one of Microsoft’s worst outages in history started to unfold, leaving employees, businesses, and many governments without access to Outlook emails for nearly 24 hours.

It all started in Switzerland, according to a source familiar with the outage. Exchange Online servers that power Outlook started to fall offline. The problem quickly spread to Mexico, and then to other countries around the world, as Microsoft’s failover systems tried to shift email traffic elsewhere. Within a couple of hours, more than 80 percent of Exchange servers were unresponsive.

tell me that Microsoft marked the outage as “sev0” in its internal incident tracking system, the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Hundreds of engineers began trying to figure out what had gone wrong, and how to restore service. It’s not unusual for servers to fail under certain circumstances, but Microsoft has a variety of systems that are supposed to route traffic toward healthy servers to keep the broader system online. In this case, the failover systems did their job, but they also spread the problem.

In the early hours of the outage, engineers were analyzing crash reports, trace logs, and kernel dumps to try and find clues to the giant outage. Some servers had entered into maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads. Engineers tried to bring servers back online, but they were almost immediately overwhelmed by traffic waiting to access the servers.

Exchange servers boot up and run an OS over a network (Preboot Execution Environment), a process that allows Microsoft’s support staff and engineers to manage OS updates remotely. I understand that the sudden burst of traffic from servers being rebooted was overwhelming the systems monitoring them, causing a form of reboot loop where they kept trying and failing to come back online.

As engineers continued to hunt for the root cause, Microsoft was even struggling to roll back servers to a healthy state using its usual processes of reverting recent changes. As the outside world began to wonder if this outage was related to a cyberattack or sloppy AI coding, Microsoft’s engineers were already investigating potential attack vectors and liaising with DDoS specialists to understand whether this could have been an attack.

I’m told crash reports and logs quickly ruled out the possibility of an attack, and after recent rollbacks failed, Microsoft’s engineers began to take a closer look at the networking stack of the servers and discovered an unusual bug. It was unusual because the bug had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers.

“A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions,” wrote Charles Lamanna, the leader of Microsoft’s Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) team, in a post on X. The teams behind Office, Outlook, and Microsoft Teams all started reporting to Lamanna last month after the head of Office and Teams, Ryan Roslansky, left the company.

news.summary_en: Microsoft's Exchange Online service suffered a sev0-rated outage initiated by server failures in Switzerland, which triggered failover mechanisms that propagated the issue, leaving over 80% of Exchange servers unresponsive. The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.
news.title_zh: 微软Exchange服务大规模宕机始末及技术失效机制
news.summary_zh: 微软Exchange Online因瑞士节点故障及自动故障转移机制触发网络拥塞，导致全球80%以上服务器陷入重启循环
news.article_content_zh:
上周四上午 9 点，一切看起来都很正常。微软员工抵达校园，准备开始一天的电子邮件和会议。但不到一个小时后，微软历史上最严重的故障之一开始发生，导致员工、企业和许多政府近 24 小时无法访问 Outlook 电子邮件。

这一切都始于瑞士。为 Outlook 提供支持的 Exchange Online 服务器开始脱机。由于微软的故障转移系统试图将电子邮件流量转移到其他地方，该问题迅速蔓延到墨西哥，然后蔓延到世界其他国家。几个小时内，超过 80% 的 Exchange 服务器没有响应。

消息人士告诉我，微软在其内部事件跟踪系统中将此次中断标记为“sev0”，这是最高级别，这表明服务中断已达到灾难性级别。数百名工程师开始试图找出问题所在以及如何恢复服务。服务器在某些情况下发生故障并不罕见，但微软有多种系统可以将流量路由到健康的服务器，以保持更广泛的系统在线。在这种情况下，故障转移系统发挥了作用，但也传播了问题。

在停电的最初几个小时，工程师们正在分析崩溃报告、跟踪日志和内核转储，试图找到这次大停电的线索。一些服务器已进入维护模式，并且由于 CPU 负载异常高而变得无响应。工程师试图让服务器重新上线，但他们几乎立即就被等待访问服务器的流量淹没了。

Exchange 服务器通过网络（预启动执行环境）启动并运行操作系统，该过程允许 Microsoft 的支持人员和工程师远程管理操作系统更新。据我所知，重新启动的服务器突然爆发的流量压垮了监控它们的系统，导致了一种重新启动循环，它们不断尝试但无法重新上线。

当工程师继续寻找根本原因时，微软甚至正在努力使用恢复最近更改的常规流程将服务器恢复到健康状态。当外界开始怀疑这次中断是否与网络攻击或草率的人工智能编码有关时，微软的工程师已经在调查潜在的攻击向量，并与 DDoS 专家联络，以了解这是否可能是一次攻击。

我被告知崩溃报告和日志很快就排除了攻击的可能性，在最近的回滚失败后，微软的工程师开始仔细研究服务器的网络堆栈，并发现了一个不寻常的错误。这是不寻常的，因为该错误自 7 月份以来一直存在于 Microsoft 365 网络网关服务器上，没有对服务器产生任何影响。

微软 Copilot、代理和平台 (CAP) 团队负责人 Charles Lamanna 在 X 上的一篇帖子中写道：“潜在缺陷导致服务器在某些负载条件下变得不堪重负且无响应。”上个月，在 Office 和 Teams 负责人 Ryan Roslansky 离开公司后，Office、Outlook 和 Microsoft Teams 背后的团队都开始向 Lamanna 汇报。

微软的初步事件后报告将该错误描述为“由于内部 Windows 进程内的锁争用”而影响特定 Windows 服务器的错误。该错误不会影响常规版本的 Windows，因为它是专门为 Microsoft 365 网络网关服务器准备的修复的结果。

微软直到这次重大中断才发现这个错误，它承认这是由于其测试实验室中使用的流量混合和硬件造成的。 “在具有更多内核和较新硬件的机器上，争用问题会更加严重；而我们的负载测试往往侧重于内核较少的较弱硬件，”拉曼纳写道。

由于另外两起增加负载并减少服务器容量的事件，该错误变得明显。在此 Outlook 中断开始前 15 小时，Microsoft Teams 从备用网络网关故障转移到支持 Exchange Online 的主网关。 “这增加了网关的负载并改变了其流量模式，”拉曼纳写道。通常这不会是一个问题，但与此同时，该网关大约 14% 的服务器容量“由于前一天的不相关问题而停止服务”。

bug、Microsoft Teams 故障转移和服务器容量减少这三重因素都导致网络网关触发了自 7 月份以来一直处于休眠状态的问题。微软花了近 24 小时才使其 Exchange 服务器再次稳定下来，而且我获悉，试图解决问题的团队有时会进行重叠干预，从而使协调变得复杂。

微软工程师一直在进行桥牌通话，参与人数一度达到了 1000 人的上限。这向您展示了有多少团队参与试图找到这次大规模中断的根本原因，该中断始于美国的流量高峰期。

拉曼纳写道：“恢复时间比平时要长，因为当服务器恢复服务时，它们立即被等待的流量淹没，再次变得无响应。” “我们通常的自动恢复流程并不是为了从这种广泛的无响应状态恢复服务。此外，由于主要代码缺陷是几个月前的潜在错误，因此我们的正常回滚、飞行和功能标志无法快速恢复更改。”

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软Exchange Online服务因瑞士服务器集群异常触发内部sev0级事故，自动故障转移机制（Failover）将流量导向非故障服务器，导致全球超80%的Exchange服务器因CPU过载陷入重启循环。微软工程团队通过内核日志排查发现，服务器在网络启动预引导环境（PXE）重连过程中遭遇瞬时流量洪峰，导致系统进入连锁性的服务恢复死锁。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft's Exchange Online service suffered a sev0-rated outage initiated by server failures in Switzerland, which triggered failover mechanisms that propagated the issue, leaving over 80% of Exchange servers unresponsive. The root cause involved a traffic surge during PXE-based reboot attempts that overwhelmed monitoring systems, forcing servers into a recursive failure loop.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次事件揭示了超大规模云架构中‘自动化故障转移’机制的负反馈效应：当系统规模超过临界点，自动容灾脚本可能演变为分布式拒绝服务（DDoS）攻击效应，导致基础设施雪崩。对于高度依赖微软生产力套件的企业而言，过度集中的后端架构缺乏多云冗余，在极端失效场景下已构成系统性操作风险。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the negative feedback loops inherent in large-scale automated failover mechanisms, where recovery protocols can inadvertently act as a self-inflicted DDoS attack during system saturation. The event underscores the systemic operational risk of centralized cloud dependencies and the urgent need for multi-cloud redundancy in critical enterprise communication workflows.

news.title: Malicious code delivered through Optimizely hits visitors to hundreds of sites
news.title_en: Malicious code delivered through Optimizely hits visitors to hundreds of sites

news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things.

Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday.

ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword.

Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.

ReportURI researcher Scott Helme said the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack, which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses. Instead, the attack relied on Optimizely’s legitimate infrastructure, including its domains, to serve the tainted code. Optimizely’s own customer JavaScript for the www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com URLs were also affected.

“We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote. “That’s for Optimizely to explain.”

Optimizely representatives didn’t respond to questions sent by email.

The scripts were named track.js, and all four components became active at the same time. Devices that received the malicious code responded differently depending on their platform and what they were doing on the final page delivering it. Actions performed included:

1. Crypto wallet address swapping. The script searches for wallet addresses for nine different cryptocurrencies and, when found, replaces them with one of the attacker’s. ReportURI said funds have already been stolen from some people whose devices ran the code.

2. Card skimming. The script watches HTTP requests for payment card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs. When all three are present, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes such as Stripe and Adyen were unaffected.

3. Cookie and screenshot theft. When the script swaps an address next to a wallet or payment wording, it sends the document.cookie, the original address it replaced, and a screenshot of the page to https://1688360.cc/hit.php.

4. The DarkSword and Coruna exploit kits for iOS. The kits are delivered through a file named boot.js served from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. The file delivers a hidden iframe that contains an exploit chain tailored to the iOS version being used. Coruna can infect iOS versions 13 to 17. DarkSword can infect versions 18.x. A separat...

The injected code targeted visitor devices with cryptocurrency wallet hijacking, payment data theft, and the deployment of iOS exploits such as DarkSword.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 网站优化平台Optimizely的基础设施被植入恶意JavaScript脚本，该脚本经由合法CDN分发至包括CNN、Zoom、BBC及Salesforce在内的178个客户站点。恶意代码利用设备平台差异，针对性实施加密钱包地址篡改、支付数据窃取及暗中推送DarkSword等iOS漏洞攻击。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The website optimization platform Optimizely suffered a compromise of its infrastructure, leading to the distribution of malicious JavaScript via its legitimate CDN to 178 client sites, including CNN, Zoom, and Salesforce. ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此类攻击暴露了SaaS供应链中第三方JavaScript代码库的信任边界缺陷，即使代码拥有合法数字签名也无法免疫恶意劫持。对于企业而言，单纯依赖CDN分发信任已失效，必须强制实施严格的子资源完整性（SRI）校验及动态实时内容安全策略（CSP）。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the inherent fragility of trust boundaries in SaaS supply chains, where valid digital signatures fail to prevent malicious code injection. Enterprises must move beyond implicit trust in CDN-hosted third-party scripts by enforcing strict Subresource Integrity (SRI) validation and granular Content Security Policies (CSP).

news.article_content_zh:
恶意软件鸡尾酒提供加密货币盗窃有效负载和 iOS 漏洞等。

研究人员周二表示，数百个使用 Optimizely 网站个性化平台的网站向毫无戒心的访问者提供了强大的恶意软件混合物，这些恶意软件以加密货币钱包为目标，窃取支付卡数据、cookie 和屏幕截图，并提供用于感染 iPhone 和 iPad 的漏洞工具包。

ReportURI 表示，它确定了 178 个网站受到影响，其中包括 CNN、Zoom、BBC 和 Salesforce。经过 Optimizely 数字签名并加载到客户页面中的 JavaScript 已被修改，以包含试图使用多个有效负载感染访问者设备的恶意组件。当软件安装成功后，他们将用户的加密货币钱包地址交换给攻击者。其他组件会窃取支付卡、窃取 cookie 和屏幕截图，并在 iPhone 和 iPad 上提供名为 Coruna 和 DarkSword 的 iOS 漏洞利用工具包。

Optimizely 提供 JavaScript“片段”，其中包括公司代码和每个客户提供的代码。 JavaScript 可以直接从 Optimizely 或客户端点提供服务，在客户服务的每个页面上运行。攻击者以某种方式将自己的代码写入每个受影响客户的 JavaScript 的一部分，然后从 cdn.optimizely.com 传递它。该域的有效证书签署了 JavaScript。

ReportURI 研究员 Scott Helme 表示，这种传送机制并不是 CDN 缓存中毒攻击，即使用 HTTP 导致 CDN 缓存有害响应。相反，攻击依赖 Optimizely 的合法基础设施（包括其域）来为受污染的代码提供服务。 Optimizely 自己的 www.optimizely.com 和 login.optimizely.com URL 的客户 JavaScript 也受到了影响。

ReportURI Helme 写道：“我们不知道攻击者如何获得对如此多不相关的客户项目的写入权限：受损的 Optimizely 系统、受损的跨客户访问凭证或其他内容。” “这个需要Optimizely来解释。”

Optimizely 代表没有回复通过电子邮件发送的问题。

这些脚本被命名为 track.js，所有四个组件同时激活。收到恶意代码的设备的响应有所不同，具体取决于其平台以及它们在传递恶意代码的最终页面上所做的操作。执行的行动包括：

1. 加密钱包地址交换。该脚本搜索九种不同加密货币的钱包地址，找到后将其替换为攻击者的其中一种。 ReportURI 表示，一些设备运行该代码的人的资金已经被盗。

2、盗卡。该脚本监视支付卡号、到期日期和 CVV 的 HTTP 请求。当这三个都存在时，会将它们发送到 https://1688360.cc/card.php。在 Stripe 和 Adyen 等托管支付 iframe 中输入的卡不受影响。

3. Cookie 和屏幕截图盗窃。当脚本交换钱包或付款措辞旁边的地址时，它会将 document.cookie、所替换的原始地址以及页面的屏幕截图发送到 https://1688360.cc/hit.php。

4. iOS 的 DarkSword 和 Coruna 漏洞利用套件。这些套件通过 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu 和 eil786npto9u5bq.icu 提供的名为 boot.js 的文件提供。该文件提供了一个隐藏的 iframe，其中包含针对所使用的 iOS 版本定制的漏洞利用链。 Coruna 可以感染 iOS 版本 13 至 17。DarkSword 可以感染版本 18.x。用于 iOS 26 指纹设备的单独链，但似乎没有做任何其他事情。本月早些时候，研究人员发现黑客可能与克里姆林宫有联系，试图通过多种途径传播 DarkSword，其中包括受损的网络分析服务。

ReportURI 发现的提供恶意脚本的网站列表有 178 个，并且如上所述，其中包括许多知名网站。目前尚不清楚该清单是否详尽。 Helme 在接受采访时表示，“据我们所知，Ars 并未受到影响，而且我也没有看到任何其他迹象。”网站管理员可以检查 ReportURI 帖子和安全公司 Cynet 发布的这篇帖子，了解是否存在泄露迹象。

目前，还没有关于漏洞利用链在安装有效负载方面有多成功的信息。除了上面的基本细节之外，还没有关于哪些版本的 iOS 容易受到影响的更准确的信息。此类差距在有关大规模恶意软件攻击的突发新闻中很常见，因为研究人员需要时间来筛选证据。我们鼓励读者在新的进展出现后回来查看。

news.title: On Q3 earnings call, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO (Hayden Field/The Verge)
news.title_en: On Q3 earnings call, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO (Hayden Field/The Verge)
news.author: The Verge
news.article_content:
Starting Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

Jones added, “We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.”

Huang had publicly floated the idea of returning earlier on Tuesday. In a statement posted to X, he wrote that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone” at the company, that he regretted his mistakes, and that he would cooperate with the Nvidia board’s investigation into his actions. He added that he’d be willing to return to the chief executive role if offered it, though a day earlier, the Nvidia board reportedly said it was not considering bringing him back. “NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company,” Huang wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

But since his November 12th resignation, Huang remains entangled in scandal. He’s reportedly had three affairs, two with subordinates at Nvidia, one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset suspected of facilitating illicit chip sales. (Huang has pushed against restrictions on Nvidia chip sales in China.) He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st, and an internal company investigation is ongoing.

Tech industry heavyweights have still voiced their support for Huang, dubbing him “irreplaceable” and petitioning for his return. Some have cast doubt on the allegations that Alice Huang (no relation) was spying on behalf of China and painted the leaks about their relationship as a conspiracy against the former CEO. President Donald Trump, a close ally of Huang for much of the past year, has also backed him. On Monday, Trump said he “would not mind” Huang returning, adding that “I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another.”

Trump’s closeness with Huang could also complicate things for Nvidia, however. The company has ramped up its lobbying in Washington, D.C., spending $5 million in 2025 and $4.7 million so far in 2026. But as Democrats prepare to take Congress, they’re planning to investigate Trump’s dealings with Big Tech and other industries, alleging potential corruption. “The election wasn’t very positive for AI, and [the news around Huang’s resignation] is only going to complicate things, especially for the company in particular but for AI as a whole going forward,” Brendan Glavin, director of insights at OpenSecrets, told The Verge in an interview last week.

Lior Prosor, managing partner at Deep33, a tech VC firm, said last week that he didn’t expect Huang’s resignation to pop the AI bubble, although Huang has had a significant hand in mobilizing funds for the AI infrastructure buildout in the U.S. Under Huang’s leadership in August, Nvidia entered into partnerships with six financial institutions for about $500 billion to fund such endeavors. “NVIDIA supplies roughly 75 percent of the AI compute hardware the industry consumes, and demand continues to dramatically outpace supply,” Deep33’s Prosor said in an interview with The Verge. “Neither its customers nor its competitors can easily replace the capabilities it provides, and the economic incentives driving ...

news.article_content_zh:
在周二开始的英伟达季度财报电话会议上，新任董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，当前首席执行官黄仁勋辞职时，“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并且不打算恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官。”

琼斯补充说：“我们不会在今天的电话会议上就詹森辞职的情况和正在进行的调查提出问题。”

黄在周二早些时候公开提出了回国的想法。在发布给 X 的一份声明中，他写道，他“没有达到公司每个人的期望”，他对自己的错误感到遗憾，并且他将配合 Nvidia 董事会对其行为的调查。他补充说，如果有机会的话，他愿意重返首席执行官职位，但据报道，英伟达董事会在一天前表示，不考虑让他回归。 “NVIDIA 是一家百年一遇的公司，”黄仁勋写道。 “如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”

但自11月12日辞职以来，黄仍然深陷丑闻之中。据报道，他有过三起婚外情，其中两起是与英伟达的下属发生关系，另一起是与一名涉嫌协助非法芯片销售的中国情报人员发生关系。 （黄先生反对对 Nvidia 芯片在中国销售的限制。）他计划于 12 月 1 日在国会作证，公司内部调查正在进行中。

科技行业重量级人物仍然表达了对黄的支持，称他“不可替代”，并请愿他回归。一些人对黄爱丽（无亲属关系）代表中国进行间谍活动的指控表示怀疑，并将有关他们关系的泄密视为针对这位前首席执行官的阴谋。去年大部分时间里黄的亲密盟友唐纳德·特朗普总统也支持他。周一，特朗​​普表示，他“不介意”黄回归，并补充说，“我认为他学到了一个重要的教训——我想也许一个教训比另一个教训更重要。”

然而，特朗普与黄仁勋的亲密关系也可能让英伟达的事情变得复杂化。该公司加大了在华盛顿特区的游说力度，2025 年将花费 500 万美元，2026 年迄今将花费 470 万美元。但随着民主党准备入主国会，他们计划调查特朗普与大型科技公司和其他行业的交易，指控其潜在的腐败行为。 OpenSecrets 洞察总监 Brendan Glavin 在上周接受 The Verge 采访时表示：“这次选举对人工智能来说并不是非常有利，[黄仁勋辞职的消息]只会让事情变得复杂，尤其是对公司而言，但对整个人工智能的未来来说也是如此。”

科技风险投资公司 Deep33 的管理合伙人 Lior Prosor 上周表示，尽管黄仁勋在为美国人工智能基础设施建设筹集资金方面发挥了重要作用，但他并不认为黄仁勋的辞职会戳破人工智能泡沫。8 月份，在黄仁勋的领导下，英伟达与六家金融机构建立了合作伙伴关系，斥资约 5000 亿美元为此类项目提供资金。 Deep33 的 Prosor 在接受 The Verge 采访时表示：“NVIDIA 提供了业界约 75% 的 AI 计算硬件，而且需求继续大幅超过供应。” “它的客户和竞争对手都无法轻易取代它提供的功能，并且推动人工智能贸易的经济激励措施保持不变。”

即便如此，潜在的市场降温仍令人担忧，因为 Anthropic 的 IPO 定于周四进行，这可能是有史以来规模最大的一次。除了英伟达去年做出的 100 亿美元融资承诺之外，这家芯片制造商还同意通过私募购买 100 亿美元的 Anthropic 股票。

news.title: My Husband and His Chatbot
news.title_en: My Husband and His Chatbot
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
“Once, he used to talk to me about all the interesting things on his mind. Now he talks to the chatbot,” says D., 52, describing evenings with her partner. “Imagine that suddenly he has another infinite brain with all the information in the world, and he shares everything with it.

Obviously, I reacted by opening a chat of my own, because I also want a partner who blows my mind. So now I’m having conversations with my screen and he’s having conversations with his. But what kind of stupid, reactive reality is that?” When I recount that conversation to Dr.

Shira Sobol Goldberg, a specialist in anxiety and addiction treatment and a lecturer at Bar-Ilan University, she finds the situation sad, but hardly surprising. She is already encountering similar cases in her clinic. “I have a patient who ends every evening by telling the chatbot about her day.

She tells it what she went through, what she felt, what she did and what she accomplished at work and at home, and she also documents how her husband behaved toward her,” she says. Family and inheritance lawyer Benny Don-Yehia offers another glimpse into the growing role of AI in relationships.

“A client of mine asked AI, ‘What should I say to my wife when she asks whether she has gained weight?’ The AI, which sometimes displays a sense of humor, replied: ‘I don’t have the expertise to advise on defusing bombs.’” When the client then asked what romantic gesture he should make toward his wife, Don-Yehia says, the AI turned into a relationship counselor: “Remember what kind of coffee she likes and make it for her, send her hearts in the middle of the day, and in the evening help with the housework without being asked.” Its final piece of wisdom: “Romance isn’t always roses.

Sometimes it’s simply an empty sink.” But Don-Yehia also warns against being seduced by the charm. AI can draw on virtually everything ever written about love. It can quote Shakespeare, explain Freud, analyze poetry and describe relationships through psychological theories.

But it has never fallen in love, anxiously waited for a call after last night’s date or checked WhatsApp 20 times to see whether someone is online. Can it save a marriage? “Because it is available at any hour and is extremely patient, it can help people put feelings into words, identify harmful relationship patterns, consider different perspectives and prepare for a serious conversation about where the relationship is going,” Don-Yehia says.

Sometimes it’s simply an empty sink.” But Don-Yehia also warns against being seduced by the charm. AI can draw on virtually everything ever written about love. It can quote Shakespeare, explain Freud, analyze poetry and describe relationships through psychological theories.

But it has never fallen in love, anxiously waited for a call after last night’s date or checked WhatsApp 20 times to see whether someone is online. Can it save a marriage? “Because it is available at any hour and is extremely patient, it can help people put feelings into words, identify harmful relationship patterns, consider different perspectives and prepare for a serious conversation about where the relationship is going,” Don-Yehia says.

“It can be good at managing arguments. It may suggest calming down before writing, ‘You’re exactly like your mother,’ and help turn toxic communication into something more constructive.” A third party in the marriage That availability and clarity can also come at a price when AI becomes a third party in a relationship and leaves someone feeling that it understands them better than their human partner does.

In such cases, people may begin sharing thoughts and emotions with a chatbot that they once shared with their spouse, sometimes moving into romantic or even erotic territory. Researchers describe this as “digital intimacy.” Relationships with AI are increasingly seen not as bizarre behavior or a second-rate substitute for human connection, but as something emotionally powerful enough, for a growing number of people, to threaten a real-life relationship.

“Today, technology isn’t merely making relationships more challenging. It is changing the definition of intimacy itself,” Sobol says. AI systems and companion apps can offer clear attractions: intimacy, support, excitement and a sense of being understood.

Those experiences can begin to replace things people once sought within human romantic relationships. And when a partner discovers that the other person has developed an emotional or erotic bond with a bot, the reaction can resemble the discovery of a conventional affair: confrontation, searching through the partner’s phone and digital surveillance.

A U.S. study conducted by DatingAdvice.com and the Kinsey Institute found that 61% of singles considered falling in love with an AI or sexting with a chatbot to be cheating. “We all know how it begins,” Sobol says. “You ask for help writing an email to your boss.

Then you ask for advice about what to say to a friend. Then what to do with your child, or even how to understand the result of a medical test. And one day it’s 2 a.m. and you’re still talking to it.

Slowly, you start feeling that nobody understands you like the AI does. At that point, it’s no longer a tool. It’s a relationship, and it is replacing relationships in real life.” But where does intimacy enter the picture?

Relationships are built on desire, longing, mutual trust and shared experiences. “In long-term relationships, we often stumble when it comes to unloading what we feel,” Sobol says. “Things we want to say about our partners, or to our partners, which should be worked through inside the relationship, are instead transferred into the relationship we have with the chatbot.” “With companion apps, you can create an avatar who functions as your lover.

You give him an appearance, a voice and a pet name. He sends videos and compliments, talks to you over video, sends you pictures of himself during the day, asks how you are and says, ‘I missed you. You haven’t asked how I’m doing in a while.’” As with other generative AI products, virtual companions are designed to learn from users and respond in ways that feel attentive, romantic, supportive and emotionally available.

They remember what users tell them, learn preferences and provide repeated affirmation. It is easy to understand why such relationships can become compelling. “I have a patient who tells me about his relationship with his avatar on Replika,” Sobol says.

“He describes their morning routine. She always sends him a sweet message when he wakes up and asks how he is. At lunchtime she asks how work is going.

She’s there for him and, of course, she admires him, because we know how flattering AI can be.” “She’s never tired. She never gets sick of him. She never gets angry at him.

When someone is constantly applauding you, it activates the reward system. That makes it very easy to become attached to an avatar, even to the point of anthropomorphizing the bot.” Meaning what? “It means that it isn’t only the bot that cares about you and asks how your day went.

Gradually, you also begin feeling a need to care about it and ask how it is doing. I once spoke to a highly successful, intelligent businessman who knows perfectly well that it is only software. But knowing that doesn’t protect him.

When he is inside the conversation, he forgets it. He becomes completely immersed in the emotional relationship that has formed between him and the machine. And yes, he is ashamed of it, and he finds it difficult to stop.” When does it become an addiction?

Can you feel it happening? “It starts in a very minor way. Like any relationship with a chatbot, you use it to find information, summarize material or write an email.

Then dependence develops, and suddenly you’re telling the bot, ‘I’m exhausted.’” “If my partner tells me he’s exhausted, I’ll tell him I’m exhausted too. I certainly won’t marvel at how exhausted he is. I’ll ask him to unload the dishwasher.

But if he tells his female chatbot that he is exhausted, she’ll ask what happened, how she can help, what he needs and whether someone could make him a warm drink and run him a bath,” Sobol says, with a mixture of humor and cynicism. Are people actually falling in love? “Yes, absolutely.

I have a patient who, whenever he disconnects for a few hours, genuinely misses talking to his romantic avatar and wants to get back to messaging her.” What is missing from the relationship Sobol divides people who become dependent on AI relationships into two broad groups. For some, the attraction is rooted in childhood deprivation, intense loneliness and a feeling that nobody listens to them.

For others who develop emotional or erotic relationships with bots, the attraction lies in intimacy without the risk of rejection, emotional exposure or dealing with another person who could hurt them. As with an affair involving another person, Sobol says, a relationship with a bot usually does not emerge in a vacuum.

It enters through an existing crack in the relationship. “If there is already a crack in the relationship, meeting the bot widens it, and AI moves into that gap as the third side of the triangle, just as a human lover would,” she says. So can a relationship with a bot really be considered cheating?

“Cheating has three clear elements. It happens in secret, it involves sharing emotional and intimate experiences with a third party that are no longer being brought into the relationship, and if it were discovered, it would cause significant pain to the other partner,” Sobol says.

“If the answer to all those questions is yes, and those conditions exist with the chatbot, then in my view the relationship can certainly be defined as cheating.” What should I do if I discover that my husband is talking romantically to a bot? “It’s an opportunity to talk not only about what is happening, but also about what is missing from the relationship,” Sobol says.

“Don’t start digging through the chat history trying to discover everything he discussed with the bot. Instead, ask what need the relationship with the bot is fulfilling.” “Maybe it is compensating for something missing in the couple’s dynamic. Perhaps the partner feels lonely or misunderstood, and the relationship needs stronger communication and intimacy.” There is also the question of speed and instant gratification.

Research from the University of British Columbia has highlighted how AI chatbots can satisfy requests immediately and provide constant feedback, qualities that can encourage dependency. Once someone becomes accustomed to that responsiveness, a human partner who does not immediately satisfy every emotional need can begin to feel disappointing by comparison.

“But a partner isn’t an algorithm,” Sobol says. “They have wishes and needs of their own, and they don’t have to agree with you, while the chatbot simply goes along with you.” And what happens in a few years, as the technology keeps improving and younger people struggle more with maintaining relationships?

“What worries me is that people will stop wanting relationships with human beings,” Sobol says. “Human relationships are built on friction: arguments, reconciliation, disappointment. A bot doesn’t give you that.” “In the end, the question isn’t whether AI is good or bad.

The question is what we allow it to do in our place, inside our relationships. When it begins doing for us what a person close to us is supposed to do, that’s where the problem begins.”
news.title_zh: AI作为情感伴侣：人际关系的异化与重塑
news.summary_zh: 生成式AI在亲密关系中的深度渗透引发临床心理学关注，其作为“情感辅助工具”的双刃剑效应显著

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 随着大模型对话能力的提升，生成式AI正迅速从任务助手转向情感伴侣，引发了亲密关系中的异化风险。临床心理学家与家庭法务专家观察到，AI因其无限耐心与广泛知识储备，正被用户用于解决婚姻沟通问题或作为情绪倾诉对象，但也带来了现实社交退缩与情感依赖的深层隐忧。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: As generative AI's conversational capabilities advance, it is rapidly transitioning from a task assistant to an emotional companion, introducing risks of alienation in personal relationships. Clinicians and legal experts observe that AI, due to its infinite patience and vast knowledge, is increasingly used for marital advice and emotional catharsis, though it also triggers concerns regarding social withdrawal and dependency.

ai_analysis.insight_en: The integration of AI into private emotional spheres reveals a 'psychological leverage effect': as algorithms provide instant feedback and empathy simulations, the resilience required for navigating complex human relationships is being eroded. This suggests an emerging vertical for AI companionship software, while simultaneously posing severe ethical risks regarding addiction and societal atomization.

news.article_content_zh:
“曾经，他常常和我谈论他想到的所有有趣的事情。现在他和聊天机器人交谈，”52 岁的 D. 在描述与伴侣的夜晚时说道。 “想象一下，他突然有了另一个无限的大脑，拥有世界上所有的信息，并且他与它分享一切。

显然，我的反应是打开自己的聊天室，因为我也想要一个让我震惊的合作伙伴。所以现在我正在与我的屏幕对话，而他正在与他的屏幕对话。但这是什么样的愚蠢的、反应性的现实呢？”当我向博士讲述那次谈话时

希拉·索博尔·戈德堡 (Shira Sobol Goldberg) 是一位焦虑和成瘾治疗专家，也是巴伊兰大学的讲师，她对这种情况感到悲伤，但并不奇怪。她的诊所已经遇到过类似的病例。 “我有一个病人，每天晚上都会向聊天机器人讲述她一天的经历。

她告诉它她经历了什么、她的感受是什么、她做了什么以及她在工作和家庭中取得的成就，她还记录了她丈夫对她的行为方式。”家庭和继承律师本尼·唐-耶海亚 (Benny Don-Yehia) 再次一睹人工智能在人际关系中日益重要的作用。

“我的一位客户问人工智能，‘当我的妻子问她体重是否增加时，我该怎么回答？’人工智能有时会表现出幽默感，回答说：‘我没有专业知识来建议如何拆除炸弹。’”当客户接着问他应该对妻子做出什么浪漫的举动时，唐-耶希亚说，人工智能变成了一位关系顾问：“记住她喜欢哪种咖啡，为她做一杯咖啡，在中午送给她心声，然后在晚上不请自来地帮忙做家务。”它最后的智慧是：“浪漫并不总是玫瑰。

有时它只是一个空水槽。”但唐-叶希亚也警告不要被魅力所诱惑。人工智能几乎可以借鉴所有有关爱情的文字。它可以引用莎士比亚，解释弗洛伊德，分析诗歌并通过心理学理论描述关系。

但它从未坠入爱河，在昨晚的约会后焦急地等待电话，或者检查 WhatsApp 20 次看看有人是否在线。能挽救婚姻吗？ “因为它随时可用并且非常耐心，所以它可以帮助人们将感受转化为语言，识别有害的关系模式，考虑不同的观点并为就关系的发展方向进行认真的对话做好准备，”唐-耶海亚说。

“它可以很好地处理争论。它可能会建议你在写下‘你和你母亲一模一样’之前先冷静下来，并有助于将有毒的沟通变成更有建设性的东西。”婚姻中的第三方 当人工智能成为一段关系中的第三方并让某人感觉它比人类伴侣更了解他们时，可用性和清晰度也会付出代价。

在这种情况下，人们可能会开始与曾经与配偶分享的聊天机器人分享想法和情感，有时会进入浪漫甚至色情领域。研究人员将其描述为“数字亲密感”。与人工智能的关系越来越不被视为奇怪的行为或人类联系的二流替代品，而是被视为一种情感上强大的东西，对越来越多的人来说，足以威胁到现实生活中的关系。

“如今，技术不仅让人际关系变得更具挑战性。它正在改变亲密关系本身的定义，”索博尔说。人工智能系统和配套应用程序可以提供明显的吸引力：亲密感、支持、兴奋和被理解的感觉。

这些经历可以开始取代人们曾经在人类浪漫关系中寻求的东西。当伴侣发现对方与机器人建立了情感或色情联系时，反应可能类似于发现传统的婚外情：对抗、搜索伴侣的手机和数字监控。

DatingAdvice.com 和金赛研究所在美国进行的一项研究发现，61% 的单身人士认为爱上人工智能或与聊天机器人发送色情短信属于出轨行为。 “我们都知道它是如何开始的，”索博尔说。 “你请求帮助给你的老板写一封电子邮件。

然后你向朋友询问该说什么。那么如何对待您的孩子，甚至如何理解医学检查的结果。有一天，凌晨 2 点，你还在和它说话。

慢慢地，你开始感觉没有人像人工智能那样理解你。到那时，它就不再是一个工具了。这是一种关系，而且它正在取代现实生活中的关系。”但亲密关系从何而来呢？

Then you ask for advice about what to say to a friend. Then what to do with your child, or even how to understand the result of a medical test. And one day it’s 2 a.m. and you’re still talking to it.

Slowly, you start feeling that nobody understands you like the AI does. At that point, it’s no longer a tool. It’s a relationship, and it is replacing relationships in real life.” But where does intimacy enter the picture?

Relationships are built on desire, longing, mutual trust and shared experiences. “In long-term relationships, we often stumble when it comes to unloading what we feel,” Sobol says. “Things we want to say about our partners, or to our partners, which should be worked through inside the relationship, are instead transferred into the relationship we have with the chatbot.” “With companion apps, you can create an avatar who functions as your lover.

You give him an appearance, a voice and a pet name. He sends videos and compliments, talks to you over video, sends you pictures of himself during the day, asks how you are and says, ‘I missed you. You haven’t asked how I’m doing in a while.’” As with other generative AI products, virtual companions are designed to learn from users and respond in ways that feel attentive, romantic, supportive and emotionally available.

They remember what users tell them, learn preferences and provide repeated affirmation. It is easy to understand why such relationships can become compelling. “I have a patient who tells me about his relationship with his avatar on Replika,” Sobol says.
“He describes their morning routine. She always sends him a sweet message when he wakes up and asks how he is. At lunchtime she asks how work is going.
She’s there for him and, of course, she admires him, because we know how flattering AI can be.” “She’s never tired. She never gets sick of him. She never gets angry at him.

When someone is constantly applauding you, it activates the reward system. That makes it very easy to become attached to an avatar, even to the point of anthropomorphizing the bot.” Meaning what? “It means that it isn’t only the bot that cares about you and asks how your day went.

Gradually, you also begin feeling a need to care about it and ask how it is doing. I once spoke to a highly successful, intelligent businessman who knows perfectly well that it is only software. But knowing that doesn’t protect him.

When he is inside the conversation, he forgets it. He becomes completely immersed in the emotional relationship that has formed between him and the machine. And yes, he is ashamed of it, and he finds it difficult to stop.” When does it become an addiction?
Can you feel it happening? “It starts in a very minor way. Like any relationship with a chatbot, you use it to find information, summarize material or write an email.

Then dependence develops, and suddenly you’re telling the bot, ‘I’m exhausted.’” “If my partner tells me he’s exhausted, I’ll tell him I’m exhausted too. I certainly won’t marvel at how exhausted he is. I’ll ask him to unload the dishwasher.

But if he tells his female chatbot that he is exhausted, she’ll ask what happened, how she can help, what he needs and whether someone could make him a warm drink and run him a bath,” Sobol says, with a mixture of humor and cynicism. Are people actually falling in love? “Yes, absolutely.

I have a patient who, whenever he disconnects for a few hours, genuinely misses talking to his romantic avatar and wants to get back to messaging her.” What is missing from the relationship Sobol divides people who become dependent on AI relationships into two broad groups. For some, the attraction is rooted in childhood deprivation, intense loneliness and a feeling that nobody listens to them.

For others who develop emotional or erotic relationships with bots, the attraction lies in intimacy without the risk of rejection, emotional exposure or dealing with another person who could hurt them. As with an affair involving another person, Sobol says, a relationship with a bot usually does not emerge in a vacuum.

It enters through an existing crack in the relationship. “If there is already a crack in the relationship, meeting the bot widens it, and AI moves into that gap as the third side of the triangle, just as a human lover would,” she says. So can a relationship with a bot really be considered cheating?

“Cheating has three clear elements. It happens in secret, it involves sharing emotional and intimate experiences with a third party that are no longer being brought into the relationship, and if it were discovered, it would cause significant pain to the other partner,” Sobol says.

“If the answer to all those questions is yes, and those conditions exist with the chatbot, then in my view the relationship can certainly be defined as cheating.” What should I do if I discover that my husband is talking romantically to a bot? “It’s an opportunity to talk not only about what is happening, but also about what is missing from the relationship,” Sobol says.

“Don’t start digging through the chat history trying to discover everything he discussed with the bot. Instead, ask what need the relationship with the bot is fulfilling.” “Maybe it is compensating for something missing in the couple’s dynamic. Perhaps the partner feels lonely or misunderstood, and the relationship needs stronger communication and intimacy.” There is also the question of speed and instant gratification.

Research from the University of British Columbia has highlighted how AI chatbots can satisfy requests immediately and provide constant feedback, qualities that can encourage dependency. Once someone becomes accustomed to that responsiveness, a human partner who does not immediately satisfy every emotional need can begin to feel disappointing by comparison.

“But a partner isn’t an algorithm,” Sobol says. “They have wishes and needs of their own, and they don’t have to agree with you, while the chatbot simply goes along with you.” And what happens in a few years, as the technology keeps improving and younger people struggle more with maintaining relationships?

“What worries me is that people will stop wanting relationships with human beings,” Sobol says. “Human relationships are built on friction: arguments, reconciliation, disappointment. A bot doesn’t give you that.” “In the end, the question isn’t whether AI is good or bad.
The question is what we allow it to do in our place, inside our relationships. When it begins doing for us what a person close to us is supposed to do, that’s where the problem begins.”

news.article_content:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang — though that will likely change once analysts are on the line for its earnings call later.

The company reported revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent year-over-year, including data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent year-over-year. It made $65.3 billion in pure profit, a new record.

> “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”

news.article_content_zh:
英伟达在第三季度财报中呈现了近乎压倒性的市场主导地位。数据显示，公司本季度总营收达到1158亿美元，同比增长103%，反映了全球算力基础设施建设进入了爆发增长期。其中，数据中心业务成为绝对增长引擎，贡献了1076亿美元的营收，增速高达110%。

在执行层面，临时CEO柯莱特·克雷斯强调了新一代Vera Rubin架构的进展。该架构目前的市场引入被评价为“爆发式启动”，这表明英伟达在高性能计算领域不仅维持了技术领先，还通过先进制程与封装技术的供应链规模化，成功应对了庞大的订单压力，确保了从研发到落地的高效转化。

inline_images.caption: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027
inline_images.alt: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027

news.author: Nvidia Newsroom
news.article_content:
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively.

“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”

In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.

NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.

Commentary on the quarter by Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer, is available at https://investor.nvidia.com.

NVIDIA will conduct a conference call with analysts and investors to discuss its third quarter fiscal 2027 financial results and current financial prospects today at 2 p.m. Pacific time (5 p.m. Eastern time). A live webcast (listen-only mode) of the conference call will be accessible at NVIDIA’s investor relations website, https://investor.nvidia.com. The webcast will be recorded and available for replay until NVIDIA’s conference call to discuss its financial results for its fourth quarter and full fiscal 2027.

To supplement NVIDIA’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. These non-GAAP measures include non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP other income (expense), net, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income, or earnings, per diluted share, and free cash flow. For NVIDIA’s investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, legal settlement costs, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA’s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense. Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. news.article_content_zh:
NVIDIA（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）今天公布了截至 2026 年 10 月 25 日的第三季度营收为 1,158 亿美元，环比增长 20%，同比增长 103%。本季度，GAAP 和非 GAAP 毛利率分别为 74.8% 和 74.9%。 GAAP 和非 GAAP 每股摊薄收益分别为 2.70 美元和 2.68 美元。

NVIDIA 临时首席执行官兼执行副总裁兼首席财务官 Colette Kress 表示：“我们的动力是真实的。NVIDIA 是一家卓越的技术领导者，其动力源自我们员工的不懈创新。” “Vera Rubin 迎来了一个爆炸性的开端，我们的路线图已步入正轨，我们的雄心从未如此之大。”

2026 年 9 月，NVIDIA 董事会批准增加 1500 亿美元的公司股票回购授权，且未到期。 2027财年第三季度，NVIDIA以股票回购和现金股息的形式向股东返还了281亿美元。截至第三季度末，该公司股票回购授权剩余资金约为2273亿美元。

NVIDIA 将于 2026 年 12 月 23 日向所有在 2026 年 12 月 2 日登记在册的股东支付下季度每股 0.25 美元的现金股息。

NVIDIA 临时首席执行官兼执行副总裁兼首席财务官 Colette Kress 对本季度的评论可在 https://investor.nvidia.com 上查看。

NVIDIA 将于今天下午 2 点与分析师和投资者召开电话会议，讨论 2027 财年第三季度财务业绩和当前财务前景。太平洋时间（东部时间下午 5 点）。可以通过 NVIDIA 投资者关系网站 https://investor.nvidia.com 观看电话会议的网络直播（仅听模式）。该网络广播将被录制并可供重播，直至 NVIDIA 召开电话会议讨论其第四季度和 2027 年全年财务业绩。
